extracted.intended_audience: organisations (universities, research organisations, funding agencies, government/regional authorities, enterprises) and researchers applying to MSCA COFUND funding
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the rules and requirements for applying to the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) COFUND action, covering applicant/beneficiary eligibility, funding rules, researcher eligibility (doctoral and postdoctoral), project features, scoring/Seals of Excellence, and the application/submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of COFUND
rubrics_metrics.description: The COFUND action provides funding for regional, national and international programmes for training and career development, through co-funding mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spreads the MSCA’s best practices by promoting high standards and excellent working conditions; promotes sustainable training and international, interdisciplinary and inter-sectoral mobility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of COFUND — Doctoral Programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctoral Programmes: They offer research training activities to allow doctoral candidates to develop and broaden their skills and competences. They will lead to the award of a doctoral degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmes must provide research training and result in a doctoral degree; relevant when designing project scope and eligible positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of COFUND — Postdoctoral Programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral Programmes: They fund individual advanced research training and career development fellowships for postdoctoral researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for advanced research training and career development of postdoctoral researchers; determines eligibility of supported researchers and fellowship design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant legal entity eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A single legal entity in an EU Member State or a Horizon Europe Associated Country applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional partners can be included in the project (i.e., consortia are allowed but the application is submitted by a single legal entity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of organisations COFUND may work with
rubrics_metrics.description: The types of organisations COFUND may work with include government entities, regional authorities, funding agencies, universities, research organisations, enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These organisation types are considered appropriate implementers/partners for COFUND projects when preparing proposals and partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum funding per beneficiary
rubrics_metrics.description: A beneficiary can receive a maximum of €10 million per call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget planning and consortium financial arrangements must respect this cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seals of Excellence scoring threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Seals of Excellence will be awarded to applications with a total score equal to or higher than 85%, but which cannot be funded due to lack of budget available under the call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a recognition mechanism for high-scoring but unfunded proposals; applicants can use it when seeking alternative funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration and minimum recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: COFUND projects should last for up to five years and should recruit at least 3 researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project planning must ensure duration ≤5 years and recruitment of a minimum of three researchers across the programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: COFUND allowance and use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: COFUND funding helps host organisations cover for each supported researcher a fixed amount (COFUND allowance) equivalent to the minimum salary that researchers should receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allowance can be used to support any cost items of the programme; additionally, a long-term leave allowance and special needs allowance may be provided if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher nationality eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers involved in COFUND projects can be of any nationality (nationals or long-term residents of an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country, in case the main part of a Postdoctoral Fellowship is carried out in a non-associated Third Country).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nationality is not restricted, but other mobility/residency rules apply (see mobility rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum support duration for researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers are supported during a minimum of 3 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects must ensure each supported researcher has at least three months of activity funded under the COFUND project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility rule for researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should comply with the mobility rules: in general, they must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation or implementing partner for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the deadline of the co-funded programme's call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This eligibility constraint determines which researchers can be recruited for a given COFUND call; exceptions and details should be checked in call-specific documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term secondments allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers can go on short term secondments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondments are permitted as part of the training/career development activities; include secondments in project planning and budgeting as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctoral candidate eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For COFUND Doctoral Programmes: must not have a doctoral degree and should be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure recruited doctoral candidates do not already hold a doctorate and maintain enrolment throughout their participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral researcher eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For COFUND Postdoctoral Programmes: must have a doctoral degree. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree will also be considered as postdoctoral researchers and will be considered eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postdoctoral candidates should not already be permanently employed by the organisation hosting them (i.e., should not already have permanent employment at host).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on permanent employment of postdocs
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral researchers should not already be permanently employed by the organisation hosting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents recruiting permanently employed staff as COFUND fellows; check employment status when selecting candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission process and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to MSCA COFUND can be submitted at any time from the opening date of the chosen call. The completed proposal, including all annexes, should be submitted by the specified submission deadline of the chosen call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must apply on behalf of an organisation or consortium and respect the opening and deadline dates of the specific call they choose to submit to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find calls, partners and application documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can find open and forthcoming calls on our page on funding and find partners and apply through the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal. All relevant documents are available on the dedicated call page on the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal, including MSCA work programme and general annexes, guide for applicants, specific FAQs, application and evaluation forms, online manual on how to submit an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the dedicated call page for call-specific rules and required annexes; use the portal to locate partners and submission interfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: How researchers find funded vacancies (EURAXESS guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates wishing to apply for PhD and postdoctoral positions under COFUND should apply to funded COFUND projects by consulting their open vacancies advertised internationally, including on the EURAXESS portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EURAXESS lists vacancies (updated daily), provides full requirements for positions, allows direct application to institutions/projects, and gives advice on visas, pensions, taxation, recognition of qualifications and other issues related to working as a researcher abroad.
